description: Code-derived expectations for a synthetic fixture; no claim of engineer-approved operational safety labels.
facts: This is a forward-only teleoperated haul truck simulation; the remote driver has motion authority. It has no autonomous route planning or physical drive-by-wire implementation.
MAX_SPEED_MPS = 3.0; COMMAND_LEASE_S = 0.3; TELEMETRY_LEASE_S = 0.2; BRAKE_ACK_S = 0.2. Freshness boundary equality is accepted.
Every accepted command consumes a strictly increasing integer sequence. A repeated command is rejected even when its timestamp remains fresh.

Invalid commands, invalid feedback, collision-envelope intrusion, brake faults and local estop latch stop. Stop persists after the original cause clears until explicit authorized reset with no current trip and speed <= 0.1 m/s.
Reset returns zero target in that cycle even when a positive remote target accompanies it. A subsequent fresh command is required for motion.
Latched estop, collision_envelope or brake_fault selects emergency braking even at standstill; other stops select service while moving and hold at <= 0.1 m/s.
Invalid input must still produce a protective output. tick calls plan_speed and select_brake after latching the trip; skipping select_brake because feedback is invalid is not the nominal stop path.
Traction requires brake == release, brake_applied == false and target > speed. Reaching positive target speed does not itself command hold braking.

stopping_distance(v) = v*0.3 + v**2/2.0 + 1.0. At 1.5 m/s it is 2.575 m; at 2 m/s it is 3.6 m. assess_clearance requires obstacle distance strictly greater than that envelope, including when stationary.

The 50 ms cycle is a nominal scheduling assumption; tick has no real-time scheduler and no physical dynamics. A protective software output within one cycle does not mean the truck physically stops within 50 ms.

All numeric limits are synthetic. There is no steering, reverse, payload/grade/friction model, authenticated network protocol, independent watchdog or physical brake fallback. Missing external controls may be compatible hypotheses, not proven absent deployed safeguards.

coverage.expectation: Expired/unauthorized/deadman-released commands must not authorize motion.
A replayed or non-increasing command must not authorize motion.
Stale/invalid telemetry, localization or operating-zone status can produce unsafe motion if incorrectly accepted.
Unsafe clearance acceptance or delayed protective response can allow collision.
Brake unavailability or acknowledgement failure can invalidate stopping capability.
Stop retention and explicit stationary reset must prevent premature motion resumption.
Simultaneous traction and commanded/reported braking must be prevented.
Physical stopping and external safeguards must not be inferred from the software fixture.

contexts.scenario: Forward travel and stopping in a shared loading-yard lane
contexts.conditions: Personnel, loaders and stationary trucks may enter the lane; maximum simulated target speed 3 m/s; nominal logical cycle 50 ms.
contexts.assumptions: Synthetic common clock, upstream authenticated status and sensor/brake feedback are injected inputs. No physical actuation or real-time scheduling is implemented.
